Since the newest Mass Effect game has turned out not so well, I've been thinking about good sci-fi RPGs to play in its stead. Here's a few that come to mind:

Star Trek Online (2010 - present): It's set in the Star Trek universe during the early 25th century (around 140 years after Kirk and 40 years after Picard's era). It's an MMO where you start out as a Federation-allied race or a Klingon-allied race (an expansion introduced the Romulans, but you have to ally with the Feds or Klingons), but there is a strong single-player component where you go on missions to explore the galaxy and fight pretty much everyone in it. There is also user-generated content, PvE queues, and PvP queues.

The missions are a mixture of ground and space. In the ground combat you are followed around by four AI-controlled "bridge officers" who you can deck out in gear. The ground combat is not the best and the animations suck (sometimes they make Andromeda look good, to be honest).

However, the space combat is great. You control a ship from the Star Trek universe and can customize it however you want - weapons, consoles (basically like amulets in fantasy RPGs), engines, shields, etc. You can own multiple ships, but can only control one at a time (there's no party system in space). It's a freemium game and has a lot of quirks that need to be worked out, but they regularly update the game with new content. It's not perfect, but its about as good as you can get when you mix a space sim and an RPG-shooter.

Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic I and II (2003, 2005): The first one was developed by Bioware when they were good. I never played these when they came out, but a lot of my friends did and they still talk about how good they were.

Fallout 3, Fallout: New Vegas, Fallout 4 (2008, 2012, 2015): Sci-fi with a post-apocalyptic bent. Most of you have probably played Fallout 4 and New Vegas, but Fallout 3 is almost 10 years old so I figured I'd suggest it to the Voaters who might've been too young for it when it came out. It's set in DC hundreds of years after a nuclear apocalypse. I played it again a while back and was surprised to find that the graphics have held up over time.

Freelancer (2003): It's more of a space sim than an RPG, but it's still fun. You control a light fighter, heavy fighter, or a freighter as you fly through space trading with and fighting various factions (the factions are all linked so your disposition with one will have a positive or negative effect on another). It has a decent campaign, too (although I recall it left a few things unresolved).

Dishonored I and II (2012, 2016): They are steampunk, rather than traditional sci-fi, but I like them for their unique settings.

Does anyone else have any other suggestions?
